title: Open Source Intelligence Researcher
content:
Rappler are seeking an experienced Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) Researcher to join their digital forensics team. This role plays a critical part in executing digital forensics and investigative research to uncover disinformation trends and provide actionable intelligence. You will work closely with editorial units, revenue teams, and brand partners to gather, analyze, and visualize complex datasets that support investigative journalism and revenue-generating data consultancy services.

You are a data-driven investigator with a passion for uncovering the truth within complex information ecosystems. You have a sharp eye for digital footprints and the analytical rigor to incorporate technical and business requirements into deep-dive research.

As a methodical researcher, you know exactly when and why to use specific OSINT tools, always approaching a problem with a clear research goal as your driving factor. You are as comfortable diving into raw datasets and coordinating with institutional sources as you are translating findings for non-technical stakeholders.

title: Asia Editor
content:
Semafor is expanding across Asia to help decision-makers in the region and around the world make sense of the region’s rapidly shifting dynamics in trade, technology, finance, geopolitics and global power, in the primary theater where the new global economy is being built.

We want to connect the dots across this complex landscape, delivering rigorous, independent business journalism to the world’s most discerning readers and are looking for a talented journalist with deep knowledge of China and the Asia-Pacific region to help lead an expansion effort across digital platforms and live journalism.

A seasoned leader with a track record of managing teams, the successful candidate will bring a deep understanding of the economic and financial forces transforming Asia — with a focus on how China is reshaping the region and the world.

title: Editor
content:
CNN is looking for an Video Editor for Visual Investigations who will focus on craft editing. The editor incorporates a visually compelling approach to editing and producing while adhering to defined editorial and journalistic standards. The editor must be able to work effectively as part of a team, take notes and work quickly under deadlines. The editor should have ability to build graphics, annotate text and images on screen. The position requires proficiency in Adobe Premiere, After Effects, color correction, and basic audio mixing.

title: Producer
content:
The Visual Investigations Producer is a highly skilled reporter/producer with a proven track record of using OSINT and other digital forensic tools and methodologies to produce groundbreaking video journalism. Must have sharp editorial judgement to uncover original stories that expose wrongdoing and hold powerful people and institutions accountable.

They must have the ability to mine information from an array of sources and turn reporting into compelling visual products for multiple platforms. The visual investigations producer must be a self-starter, an enthusiastic employee with deep curiosity, and able to work well on a team.

title: Senior Producer
content:
The visual investigations senior producer is a highly skilled reporter/producer with a proven track record of using sharp editorial judgement to uncover original stories through data-driven reporting, video and image analysis, and other investigatory methods. They will produce video investigations that deconstruct critical moments, expose wrongdoing and hold powerful people and institutions accountable through compelling visual products for multiple platforms. They must have a proven track record of using OSINT and other digital forensic tools and methodologies to produce groundbreaking original video journalism.

Must be a self-starter, an enthusiastic employee with deep curiosity, and able to work well on a team.  The main responsibilities will include all aspects of story research and newsgathering, including visuals – whether graphics, animations, or video, setting up and producing shoots and edits and executing multiple projects simultaneously.

title: First Look: IJ WEEK World-Class Speakers and Cutting-Edge Sessions
content: With just 12 weeks left until the kickoff of IJ WEEK on October 26, the full program is taking shape. We’ll have more than 100 speakers from all around the world, featuring panel discussions with world renowned journalists exposing authoritarian regimes, workshops on telling investigative stories through maps and audio, experts talking about how to investigate tech, and fundraising and sustainability advisors discussing the future of funding. And in celebration of the 25th anniversary of the first International Gathering of Investigative Journalists, IJ Week will also feature the participation of Brant Houston (United States) and Nils Mulvad (Denmark), who co-organized that first event and later co-founded GIJN together with representatives from other organizations from around the world.

title: Do You Have ‘the OSINT Mindset’?: Try Our Quiz for Those Who Like ‘a Little Light Online Sleuthing’
content:
OSINT, visual investigations, digital sleuthing: however you refer to the field, it’s become a hugely significant part of investigative journalism in recent years. From finding initial leads, to building evidence relevant to an existing hypothesis, to verifying a piece of evidence found on social media – these skills can be used in many different ways for investigative reporting.

At the Centre for Investigative Journalism, we’ve been delivering training on these techniques for more than a decade to journalists and other researchers investigating in the public interest. What this experience has taught us, in turn, is that the core OSINT mindset is the most important learning goal.

While there is, of course, great value in learning tools and techniques that allow you to conduct online investigative research more effectively and efficiently right now, the field is especially dynamic. Good tools that work today may be behind financially inaccessible paywalls tomorrow, web infrastructure is subject to frequent change that means certain techniques become less reliable, new platforms spring up often with the potential to make whole sections of practice obsolete.

title: Building an Engaged Community through Collaboration and In-Depth Investigations, All While Maintaining a Sense of Humor
content:
“The thing we feared the most in the very beginning, given our relaxed vibe, was becoming too serious and turning into a bureaucratic office,” says Miglė Krancevičiūtė, co-founder of the Lithuanian investigative outlet Siena.

As we speak, she is leaning against a custom-printed pillow with a tongue-in-cheek quote — “financial cushion!” — from one of their recent investigations. Fans of their work, and follow-the-money anti-corruption investigations in general, can buy the cushion in their online shop for €25 (about $28).

Image: Screenshot from Siena’s online store

Founded in 2019, the nonprofit newsroom has taken part in hard-hitting investigations led by international networks, including projects like Dubai Unlocked, the FinCEN files, and the Pandora Papers, and in 2022, the outlet became one of GIJN’s members. But its core mission is to bring that networked journalism experience home to Lithuania.

To the west of the country, across the Baltic Sea, lies Sweden, where the team at Siena draws journalistic inspiration. On the other side of a forested border is Belarus, whose internationally sanctioned dictator is a target of numerous Siena investigations.

title: Aleph Pro Tutorial: How to Get the Most from OCCRP’s Updated Investigative Data Platform
content:
Our world is data. Vast amounts of data. And this data holds many stories, often buried behind a confusing collection of documents, spreadsheets, and databases. Finding patterns, trends, and the wider story requires massive swaths of data, the ability to process it, and, most importantly, making it accessible to journalists and investigators who aren’t necessarily data experts.

This is where Aleph Pro comes in. Launched in December 2025, it’s an update of Aleph — a huge data repository hosted by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) that includes hundreds of datasets, public records, and leaks from more than 180 countries, with a cross-referencing feature that enables users to search for names and companies of interest and uncover previously unknown connections. Aleph Pro has performance upgrades, a new interface, and new features.

This tipsheet explains how to get started with the Aleph Pro platform and how to make the most of its datasets, cross-referencing capabilities, and new features.
